title: EduNexus Experiment Knowledge Schema
description: Validates a single Electrical Engineering experiment knowledge file (e.g. bridge_rectifier.json, buck_converter.json). One instance of this schema describes exactly one experiment.

experiment_id.description: Stable, unique, filesystem-safe identifier. Must match the JSON file's name without extension.

experiment_name.description: Human-readable experiment title, e.g. 'Single Phase Bridge Rectifier'.

objective.description: One or two sentences stating what the experiment sets out to demonstrate.

overview.description: Explanation of the underlying concept: definition, working principle, and circuit behavior.

applications.description: Real-world / industrial applications of this concept.

components.description: Physical or logical components used in the experiment (diodes, capacitors, resistors, switches, ICs, etc.).

id.description: Short reference used elsewhere (e.g. in expected_connections.component or troubleshooting entries), e.g. 'D1', 'C1'.

nodes.description: Map of physical node/socket number (as it appears on the hardware board, e.g. in socket_positions_*.json) to its role and description. Keys are node numbers as strings.

role.description: Functional role of this node in the circuit.

description.description: Short human-readable explanation of what this node physically is.

expected_connections.description: The complete, correct wiring for this experiment. Every entry must use real node numbers from the nodes object (or the corresponding socket_positions file) — never placeholder values.

id.description: Unique connection identifier within this experiment, e.g. 'C1'.

from.description: Real node/socket number where this connection starts. Must not be a placeholder such as 0 unless 0 is a genuine node label on the hardware.

to.description: Real node/socket number where this connection ends. Must not be a placeholder such as 0 unless 0 is a genuine node label on the hardware.

component.description: Component or terminal this connection relates to, e.g. 'Diode D1' or component id from the components array.

purpose.description: Why this connection exists in the circuit.

effect_if_wrong.description: Practical consequence if this connection is missing, extra, or reversed.

recommendation.description: Corrective guidance the AI teacher should give the student.

common_mistakes.description: Typical wiring errors students make for this connection.

troubleshooting.description: Optional per-connection diagnostic tip (e.g. multimeter check). General experiment-level troubleshooting belongs in the top-level troubleshooting array.

else.description: from:0,to:0 placeholders are rejected by this schema — real node numbers are required.

waveform.description: Expected input/output signal behavior for this experiment.

input.description: Description of the expected input waveform, e.g. 'sine, 50Hz'.

output.description: Description of the expected output waveform, e.g. 'full-wave pulsating DC'.

ripple_description.description: Optional description of ripple behavior, where applicable.

calculations.description: Formulas and reference calculations relevant to this experiment.

notes.description: Optional clarifying notes about when/how to apply the formulas.

troubleshooting.description: General, experiment-level fault scenarios not tied to a single connection (e.g. short circuit, reverse polarity).

viva_questions.description: Reference question/answer bank used by viva mode.

safety.description: Safety precautions specific to this experiment.

expected_observations.description: What a correctly-run experiment should produce, in observable terms (e.g. measured voltage ranges).

practical_applications.description: Industry or real-world use cases for this circuit/experiment.
